title: Evaluation of really good grammatical error correction

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the performance of rule-based, MT-based, and LLM-based Grammatical Error Correction (GEC) systems using reference-based metrics, reference-free metrics, and human judgments to demonstrate how certain metrics inherently favor either conservative minimal edits or specific neural language model architectures.

Evaluating GEC systems against traditional human references to highlight how annotator instructions to stay close to the original text (minimal edits) bias the evaluation against models capable of extensive, fluent paraphrasing.
